body:
At first glance, this makes some intuitive sense, since Node2D's Transform2D and Node3D's Transform3D are ordered in `Position, Rotation, Scale`. In those nodes, `Position` does come before `Scale`, and `Scale` is like `Size`.
![Godot_v4 4-dev6_win64_sdDjZ9sM7W](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fae9678-6c99-4c5b-a23d-1467b89de565)
![Godot_v4 4-dev6_win64_R0ZI1SRtLl](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82d220a5-3489-4fed-a00c-f0ae2474f656)

On the other hand, if you look at Control, it currently first lists its `Size`, then it lists `Position, Rotation, and Scale` in the same order as Node2D and Node3D. So the existing order already keeps consistency pretty well, by preserving the order of `Position, Rotation, and Scale`.
![Godot_v4 4-dev6_win64_oDk9nZTQPb](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d93a50e-35ef-4e50-8183-6b4ae9b66726)

One might also consider an order of `Position, Rotation, Size, Scale`, or `Position, Rotation, Scale, Size`.

Remember that for Controls, `Position` and `Size` are the two things which you will be most often editing, and `Rotation` and `Scale` should *usually* not be edited in typical UI layouts.

There is *some* cost to changing the default order, as you break some existing muscle memory. So since the existing order follows some logic, we probably shouldn't change it unless the alternative is clearly better.

After making these comparisons to other nodes, I'm not actually sure what the ideal order for the properties is. Hopefully these comparisons are at least helpful for considering the pros and cons...?

@tetrapod00 thanks for checking it. makes sense.

Do you think this is a case to open an Issue/discussion to debate what you mentioned or should I just leave here since it's visible anyway for anyone who wants to chip in? Don't want to "overcrowd" the issues list xD

I like this proposal since I always find myself changing the scale of a node when I actually want to change its position (= it feels natural to me that "position" should come first).

However, @tetrapod00 does make a good point : breaking consistency across menus would not be ideal.

I'm wondering if this could be a case where the order could be made configurable ? (as an editor setting ?)
